name: Icchey Gaon
tagline: A 1,770 m homestay ridge between Kalimpong and Pedong
meta_description: Icchey Gaon (Icche Gaon), about 1,770 m near Kalimpong: Kanchenjunga dawns, walks to Ramitey Dara and Damsang fort, birds, homestays, costs and access.
summary: Icchey Gaon, also spelled Icche Gaon or Echey Gaon, is a homestay village at about 1,770 m (5,800 ft), roughly 18 km from Kalimpong and 2.5 km above Ramdhura. It has a clear Kanchenjunga view, forest walks to Ramitey Dara and Damsang fort, and good birds. Two nights is ideal.

local_story.title: A village of walks between three histories
paras: Icchey Gaon sits on a forested ridge between Kalimpong and Pedong, and the walks from it lead straight into the region's history. About 6 km away is Damsang, where the Lepcha chief Gaeboo Achyok held out against the Bhutanese in the late 17th century. A little further is Pedong's Sangchen Dorjee monastery, built some 300 years ago under Bhutanese rule. Below runs the Reshi river and the border with Sikkim, along the line of the old trade road to Tibet.

The village itself is a farming settlement of Nepali-speaking families, with terraces of maize and vegetables, cardamom in the shade and forest of oak, pine, maple and tree ferns on the slopes above. We have not found a reliable account of what its name means, and locals give different answers, so we will not offer one.

Homestays have grown here as travellers looked for quieter alternatives to Kalimpong, and the village has kept a small scale. Its height, about 250 m above Ramdhura, gives it a wider view: on clear mornings the Kanchenjunga range spreads along the horizon beyond the Teesta valley.

did_you_know: Icchey Gaon sits at about 1,770 m (5,800 ft), roughly 520 m higher than Kalimpong town and 250 m above neighbouring Ramdhura.
Damsang fort, the 17th-century stronghold of the Lepcha chief Gaeboo Achyok, is about 6 km from Icchey Gaon.
The forests around Icchey Gaon hold tree ferns, orchids, oaks, pines and maples, with flycatchers, sunbirds, woodpeckers and emerald cuckoos among the birds.
intro: Icchey Gaon is the walker's choice among the villages north-east of Kalimpong. From your homestay, trails lead to Ramitey Dara for the Teesta's bends, to Damsang fort, to Ramdhura and Sillery Gaon, and into forest full of birds. In between, you sit in the garden and watch Kanchenjunga.

It is close to Kalimpong, under an hour by car, and costs about the same as its neighbours: ₹1,400–2,200 per person with meals. The village is small and spread out, with homestays of different standards; ask about attached bathrooms and hot water. Two nights give you one day of walking and two chances at a clear dawn.

highlights.title: Kanchenjunga along the horizon
highlights.text: At about 1,770 m, Icchey Gaon has one of the wider views among the villages near Kalimpong. On clear mornings from October to April the range spreads across the horizon beyond the Teesta valley.

highlights.title: Walk to Damsang fort
highlights.text: About 6 km to the ruins of the Lepcha chief Gaeboo Achyok's fort, through forest and farmland, with a guide. A half-day walk into the founding story of the Lepcha people.

highlights.title: Ramitey Dara
highlights.text: The viewpoint above the Teesta's long series of bends, reached on trails from Icchey Gaon or Sillery Gaon. Go in the morning, before haze, with a local guide.

highlights.title: Forest birding
highlights.text: Oak, pine, maple and tree-fern forest around the village holds flycatchers, sunbirds, woodpeckers and, in spring, the calls of emerald cuckoos. Walk the lanes at first light.

highlights.title: Village-to-village walks
highlights.text: Ramdhura is 2.5 km away and Sillery Gaon a longer walk. Send your bags by car and walk between homestays for a slow, cheap trip.

how_to_reach.text: From Kalimpong a car costs about ₹1,300–2,000 one way and takes 45 minutes to an hour. From NJP or Bagdogra about ₹4,000–5,500, roughly 89 km and 3.5–4 hours via Kalimpong. NH10 has had closures since October 2023; check current status before you travel.
There is no regular shared jeep to Icchey Gaon. Take a shared jeep from Siliguri to Kalimpong (₹200–300) and then a local car, or ask your homestay to arrange a pickup.
Icchey Gaon is about 2.5 km and 45 minutes' walk uphill from Ramdhura along the ridge. Many travellers combine the two villages.

where_to_stay: Icchey Gaon has family-run homestays and small cottages spread along the ridge, at about ₹1,400–2,200 per person with dinner and breakfast. Standards vary: some have wood-panelled rooms with attached bathrooms and geysers, others are simpler with shared facilities. Ask for a room facing the Kanchenjunga side. There are no hotels. Ramdhura, 2.5 km below, and Sillery Gaon, further east, have similar homestays; Kalimpong, under an hour away, has government lodges.
tips: Plan one full day for a walk to Damsang fort or Ramitey Dara with a local guide.
Ask for a room on the view side and confirm hot water before booking.
Carry cash; there is no ATM and the network for UPI is patchy.
Pack layers: nights drop to around 2–6 °C in winter.
Village roads can be blocked or slippery after heavy rain: check current status before you travel.

experiences.title: Hike from Icchey Gaon to Damsang fort
experiences.summary: Walk about 6 km through forest and farmland to the ruined stronghold of Gaeboo Achyok, the 17th-century Lepcha chief who fought the Bhutanese for these hills. A half-day hike with history at the end.
body: Damsang Gadi, the fort of the Lepcha chief Gaeboo Achyok, stands in ruins on a ridge about 6 km from Icchey Gaon. In the second half of the 17th century, Achyok ruled a Lepcha principality from here and resisted the Bhutanese, allying with Tibet. He was eventually captured and executed. The fort is usually dated to 1690; Lepcha lore says spirits carried its round stones up from the Reshi river.

The walk follows village paths and forest trails, with some steep sections. Allow 2–2.5 hours each way, and take a local guide, about ₹600–1,000, because paths branch and the fort is easy to miss in the trees. On the way you pass farms, cardamom groves and patches of old forest with good birds.

At the fort you will find low walls and scattered dressed stones, and views towards Pedong and Sikkim. Do not climb on the walls. Carry water and lunch. On 20 December, Lepchas gather here for Achyok's birth anniversary; if you come that day, be respectful and keep to the edges.

faqs.q: How far is Damsang fort from Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: About 6 km, roughly 2–2.5 hours each way on foot on village paths and forest trails. You can also drive part of the way via Pedong and walk the last stretch. A guide costs about ₹600–1,000.

faqs.q: Is the Damsang fort hike difficult?
faqs.a: It is moderate: a half-day walk with some steep and slippery sections, especially after rain. Reasonably fit walkers manage it comfortably. Wear shoes with grip and carry water. Avoid it in the monsoon, when leeches and mud make it hard.

faqs.q: Why is Damsang fort important?
faqs.a: It was the stronghold of Gaeboo Achyok, the most celebrated Lepcha hero, who fought Bhutanese expansion in the late 17th century. For the Lepcha community it is a symbol of their history in these hills, and they gather there every 20 December.

experiences.title: Ramitey Dara from Icchey Gaon
experiences.summary: Walk with a guide to Ramitey Dara, the viewpoint where the Teesta winds in a long chain of bends far below, often counted as 14. Morning light, a forest trail and a view that is hard to believe.
body: Ramitey Dara is the best-known viewpoint in the villages north-east of Kalimpong. From its ridge, you look down on the Teesta, the river that drains nearly all of Sikkim, as it loops through its valley in a long series of bends, often counted as 14. Behind, the hills of Sikkim rise in ridges.

From Icchey Gaon the walk takes about 1.5–2 hours each way on trails through forest and farmland. Take a local guide, about ₹600–1,000, as the paths are not marked. Some people combine it with Sillery Gaon, which is closer to the viewpoint, and get a car back.

Go early: the river's bends are clearest in the morning, before haze and cloud fill the valley. October and November are best. Carry water and snacks, as there is nothing at the top but prayer flags and the view.

faqs.q: Is Ramitey Dara closer to Icchey Gaon or Sillery Gaon?
faqs.a: It is closer to Sillery Gaon, about 3 km away. From Icchey Gaon the walk is longer, about 1.5–2 hours each way. Many walkers go from Icchey Gaon to Ramitey Dara and on to Sillery Gaon, then take a car back.

faqs.q: What is the best time to see the Teesta from Ramitey Dara?
faqs.a: Early morning from October to December, when the air is clear and the river's bends stand out. Later in the day haze softens the view. In the monsoon, cloud often fills the valley completely.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for Ramitey Dara?
faqs.a: We recommend one from Icchey Gaon. Trails branch and are not marked, and a local guide also knows the best spot for the view. Guides cost about ₹600–1,000 for the trip.

experiences.title: Dawn birding in Icchey Gaon's forest
experiences.summary: Walk the forest edges around Icchey Gaon at first light among oak, pine, maple and tree ferns, for flycatchers, sunbirds, woodpeckers and, in spring, the call of the emerald cuckoo.
body: Icchey Gaon's forests are a mix of oak, pine, maple and tree ferns, with orchids on the trunks. That variety brings good birds within a few minutes' walk of the homestays. At first light, look for flycatchers on exposed perches, sunbirds at flowers, and mixed flocks of tits and warblers moving through the canopy.

Woodpeckers drum on dead trunks, and barbets call from the treetops. In spring, from April to May, listen for the emerald cuckoo, a small, brilliant green bird more often heard than seen. Walk slowly along the village lanes and forest edges, stopping where trees meet fields.
A local guide costs about ₹500–1,000 for a morning. Carry binoculars, wear muted colours and keep voices low. After the walk, breakfast in the garden with the Kanchenjunga view is the best reward.

faqs.q: What birds can I see in Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: Flycatchers, sunbirds, woodpeckers, barbets, tits, warblers and, in spring, emerald cuckoos are among the birds of the village forests. A good morning with a guide can produce several dozen species.

faqs.q: When is the best time for birdwatching in Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: March to May, when birds are singing and breeding, is best. October to December is also good, with clear mornings. Start at first light and finish by about 9 am.

faqs.q: Do I need special gear for birding here?
faqs.a: Binoculars are the one essential. A field guide or app helps with names, and a camera with a long lens if you photograph. Wear muted colours and comfortable shoes with grip.

experiences.title: Kanchenjunga dawn from an Icchey Gaon garden
experiences.summary: At about 1,770 m, Icchey Gaon looks over the Teesta valley to the full Kanchenjunga range. Step into your homestay garden before sunrise and watch the snow catch the light.
body: Icchey Gaon is higher than Kalimpong and Ramdhura, and its ridge looks across the Teesta valley and the hills of Sikkim to the Kanchenjunga range. On clear mornings from October to April, the summit, 8,586 m high and well over 80 km away, catches the sun a few minutes before everything else.

Ask your hosts to wake you 30 minutes before sunrise: around 5.30 am in October and March, after 6 am in December and January. Wrap up warmly; winter dawns are close to freezing. Most homestays have a garden or terrace facing the range, so you will not need to walk.
Mid-October to early December gives the best chance of a clear sky. Stay two nights for two chances. If the peaks are hidden, wait 20–30 minutes after sunrise, when cloud often lifts briefly.

faqs.q: Is the Kanchenjunga view good from Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: Yes, it is one of the wider views among the villages near Kalimpong, thanks to the height of about 1,770 m. On clear mornings the range spreads across the horizon beyond the Teesta valley. The best months are October to April.

faqs.q: Which month is best for the view from Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: Late October to early December gives the clearest skies. February and March are also good. January is clear but very cold at dawn. From June to September cloud usually hides the peaks.

faqs.q: Do all Icchey Gaon homestays have a view?
faqs.a: Not all. The village is spread over a slope, and some houses face away from the range or are screened by trees. Ask for a room or garden with a Kanchenjunga view when you book.

faqs.q: How do I reach Icchey Gaon from Kalimpong?
faqs.a: By reserved car, about 18 km and 45 minutes to an hour, for ₹1,300–2,000 one way. There is no regular shared jeep. Your homestay can arrange a pickup from Kalimpong's Motor Stand.

faqs.q: Is it Icchey Gaon, Icche Gaon or Echey Gaon?
faqs.a: All three spellings refer to the same village at about 1,770 m near Kalimpong. You will see each on maps, signs and booking sites. Search with all of them when looking for homestays.

faqs.q: What is the homestay cost in Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: About ₹1,400–2,200 per person per night with dinner and breakfast, depending on the room and season. Rates rise in October, December and on long weekends. Lunch is extra, around ₹150–250.

faqs.q: How many days should I stay in Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: Two nights is ideal: one full day for a walk to Damsang fort or Ramitey Dara, and two chances at a clear Kanchenjunga dawn. Add a night in Ramdhura or Sillery Gaon for a slow village circuit.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: October to December for clear views and dry trails, and March to May for birds and spring flowers. January and February are cold but often clear. From June to September it is wet and misty, with leeches on forest paths.

faqs.q: Is Icchey Gaon good for trekking?
faqs.a: Yes, for day walks. Trails lead to Damsang fort, about 6 km, Ramitey Dara, Ramdhura and Sillery Gaon. These are village and forest paths rather than high treks, best with a local guide for ₹600–1,000.

faqs.q: Can I see Kanchenjunga from Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days from October to April, best at dawn. The range lies beyond the Teesta valley and the hills of Sikkim. Ask for a homestay with a view-facing room or garden.

faqs.q: Is Icchey Gaon suitable for families?
faqs.a: Yes, for families who enjoy simple stays. Choose a homestay with attached bathrooms and hot water. Short walks to Ramdhura suit children; the Damsang and Ramitey Dara walks suit older children and teenagers.

faqs.q: Is there network in Icchey Gaon?
faqs.a: Patchy. Jio and Airtel work in parts of the village, and data is slow. Download maps and tickets in Kalimpong before you come, and carry cash for homestays and guides.
